verses: لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ
تَنَزَّلُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِم مِّن كُلِّ أَمْرٍ

leads.title: Passover law, matzot, the night of the firstborn, departure from Egypt ↔ The Night of Decree
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: The exodus night is a 'night of watching' for God and for Israel through the generations (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Passover law, matzot, the night of the firstborn, departure from Egypt: No one may leave the house until morning on the night of the destroyer; The people carry their unleavened dough in kneading-troughs on their shoulders; Israel's stay in Egypt lasts 430 years to the very day; Festival days are holy convocations on which no work is done except preparing food; Small households join neighbors to share one sacrificial lamb; Defeated king asks the departing prophet to bless him too; Leaven must be removed from houses; whoever eats it is cut off; A mixed multitude (erev rav) of non-Israelites leaves Egypt with Israel; The spring exodus month becomes the first month of the year; No bone of the paschal sacrifice may be broken; No uncircumcised foreigner may eat the Passover; circumcised slaves and converts may; An unblemished yearling lamb selected on the tenth and slaughtered at twilight on the fourteenth; and 18 more.

Only in The Night of Decree: On a holy night the angels and the Spirit descend by their Lord's permission with every command; it is peace until dawn; Scripture sent down on the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr), better than a thousand months; A day in God's courts is better than a thousand elsewhere; better a doorkeeper than dwell in tents of wickedness; Rhetorical formula 'And what will make you know what X is?' (wa ma adraka ma) introducing an eschatological term.

leads.title: Psalm 84, how lovely are your dwellings; the sparrow at the altar ↔ The Night of Decree
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/08-hb-quran.yaml).
Shared motifs, rarest first: A day in God's courts is better than a thousand elsewhere; better a doorkeeper than dwell in tents of wickedness (weight 7.7). Pair score 7.7.

Only in Psalm 84, how lovely are your dwellings; the sparrow at the altar: YHWH God is called a sun (shemesh) and a shield; Soul longs and faints for the courts of YHWH, the living God; Baca / Bakka on the pilgrims' way or as the House [divergence between the texts]; Sparrow and swallow find a nest for their young at God's altars; Wish to dwell in God's tent or house forever; Pilgrims passing through the Valley of Baca (weeping/balsam) make it a place of springs; God gives strength to his king and exalts the horn of his anointed (messiah); The House (Kaaba) made a place of return and security for mankind; Pilgrims go from strength to strength until each appears before God in Zion; Genealogy of Korah and his sons; Heading assigns the psalm to a Levitical singer or guild (Jeduthun, Asaph, sons of Korah, Heman, Ethan).

Only in The Night of Decree: On a holy night the angels and the Spirit descend by their Lord's permission with every command; it is peace until dawn; Scripture sent down on the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr), better than a thousand months; The exodus night is a 'night of watching' for God and for Israel through the generations; Rhetorical formula 'And what will make you know what X is?' (wa ma adraka ma) introducing an eschatological term.
